\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Discrete Approximation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Bobkov.DiscreteApproximation
\section{Overview}
Lipschitz derivative bounds give quadratic linearization estimates. Applied to normalized Boolean blocks, these estimates compare discrete half-differences with partial derivatives and quantify the vanishing approximation error.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic linearization remainder]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_linearization_remainder_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and $f:E\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $D(x):E\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $x\mapsto D(x)$ is $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm, where $C\ge0$. For all $x,y\in E$, $|f(y)-f(x)-D(x)(y-x)|\le C\|y-x\|^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Half-increment approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_half_increment_sub_derivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_linearization_remainder_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and $f:E\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $D(x):E\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $x\mapsto D(x)$ is $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm, where $C\ge0$. For $x,v\in E$ and $h\in\mathbb R$, $|(f(x+hv)-f(x))/2-(h/2)D(x)v|\le(C/2)h^2\|v\|^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Updating a normalized Boolean block]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolBlocks_update}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{4}
For $n,m\ge0$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times m}$, define $S_m(x)_k=m^{-1/2}\sum_{l=1}^m(-1)^{x_{kl}}$, interpreting division by zero as zero. If $x^{ij\leftarrow b}$ replaces bit $(i,j)$ by $b$, then $S_m(x^{ij\leftarrow b})=S_m(x)+\bigl((-1)^b-(-1)^{x_{ij}}\bigr)m^{-1/2}e_i$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th coordinate vector.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Block half-difference approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_normalizedBoolBlocks_half_difference_sub_derivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_half_increment_sub_derivative_le,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolBlocks_update,BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign,BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_false,BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_true}
\difficulty{5}
For $n,m\ge0$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times m}$, define $S_m(x)_k=m^{-1/2}\sum_{l=1}^m(-1)^{x_{kl}}$, interpreting division by zero as zero. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative family $D(z)$ that is globally $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm on $\mathbb R^n$, with $C\ge0$. For any bit $(i,j)$, $\left|\frac{f(S_m(x^{ij\leftarrow0}))-f(S_m(x^{ij\leftarrow1}))}{2}-\frac{D(S_m(x))e_i}{\sqrt m}\right|\le2C/m$.
\end{lemma}
